intro: I'm a self-taught designer from Jaipur with a degree in computer engineering. By day I make advertising and brand narratives. Outside the office I make art, mostly by turning everyday objects into small vessels of emotion and meaning.

At Grofers, which became Blinkit, I spent over six years in marketing design: integrated campaigns around the app's recurring sale events, social content, app visual identities, and the hiring and development of a creative team. I left as Associate Director in October 2021.

Since then I've led Communication Design at Razorpay across Payments, RazorpayX and POS. The work is brand films, keynote videos, landing pages, sales decks, social campaigns and product imagery, held together by one visual system and a way of telling stories that starts from data, consumer interviews and what past campaigns taught us.

A lot of that work is now AI-native. *Trial of the Century*, the animal-courtroom film for RazorpayX Payroll, won Generative AI at the Shorty Awards. *Break To Build* turned one photograph of each of thirty founders into thirty ad films. Both ran as repeatable production systems rather than one-offs, and the design team now uses four in-house AI tools on live campaigns.

items.note: Leads Communication Design across Payments, RazorpayX and POS: brand films, keynote videos, landing pages, sales decks, social campaigns and product imagery. Established a deck design language now used across more than ten product lines and business units.
Integrated advertising for recurring sale events, social campaigns and app visual identities. Hired and developed the creative team and directed external production partners.
Design was already happening alongside the degree: a CopyPress Infographic Designer certificate followed in December 2013.

leadership.label: On creative leadership
leadership.title: Notes from running an in-house design team.
leadership.intro: From a 2024 post on planning the year for in-house design teams. The ideas I still work from:

items.title: Keep widening the toolkit
items.body: Video and animation, 3D in Blender and Spline, and AI tools such as ChatGPT, Midjourney, Ideogram and Runway. Continuous learning keeps a team competitive, and engaged.

items.title: Make goals measurable
items.body: Use analytics not only to validate creative work but to show how it contributes to the company. Aim for content that resonates, from social buzz to booklets that win over the most numbers-minded colleague.

items.title: Build a culture that can take risks
items.body: Turn brainstorms from dreaded meetings into hubs of collaboration, where trying something bold does not mean fearing failure.

items.title: Design for the business, not just the brief
items.body: Work in step with the brand marketing team so the output reflects company goals, not only creative ambition.

studio.label: After hours
studio.title: The studio at night.
studio.body:
In my creative studio I work on AI art, stop-motion animation and found-object art, and make fun, quirky content for platforms, especially Instagram. The work runs from introspective musings to whimsical one-liners.

Two AI experiments from 2023, built on Stable Diffusion and ControlNet, live in the Lab.

items.caption: On stage at the Reimagine Awards

items.a: Vibhor Mathur is a creative director and design leader based in Bengaluru, India. He is Communication Design Senior Manager at Razorpay, where he leads Communication Design across Payments, RazorpayX and POS. From 2015 to 2021 he was at Grofers (now Blinkit), leaving as Associate Director, Marketing Design. He is a self-taught designer from Jaipur with a B.Tech in computer engineering.

items.q: What can I hire Vibhor for?
items.a: Creative and art direction for brand films, launch videos and campaigns; AI-native film and campaign production; interactive landing pages and games; building and leading in-house design teams and visual systems; custom AI design tools for studios; and design mentoring or workshops on AI in design.

items.q: What has he made with AI?
items.a: Trial of the Century, an AI film for RazorpayX Payroll, won Generative AI at the Shorty Awards. Break To Build turned one photograph of each of thirty founders into thirty ad films. Backing India's Start-Up Champions produced 81 television films, a newspaper front page and more than 200 social posts for 20 founders with no cameras, sets or lights. Back in the Ring is a fully in-house, fully AI-made cinematic trailer for Razorpay Netbanking.

items.q: What awards has his work won?
items.a: Shorty Awards 2026: Winner, Generative AI; Gold Honor, Financial Services; Finalist, Community Engagement, for Trial of the Century. Kyoorius Creative Awards 2026: First List for Film Craft and for Use of Technology and AI. ET Brand Disruption Awards 2026: Gold, Most Disruptive Creative and Design Team, and Silver, Most Disruptive B2B Campaign.

items.q: What results has his work delivered?
items.a: Backing India's Start-Up Champions reached 8.1 million unique viewers and lifted purchase intent by 133 percent. Trial of the Century earned more than 2.1 million impressions. The MoneySaver Export Account launch reached 29.1 million in media.

items.q: What AI tools has his design team built?
items.a: The Razorpay design team built and uses a Cinematography Tool, a Product Image Generator, an Advanced Image Editor and a Founder Image Generator on live campaigns, all with proper interfaces rather than blank prompt boxes. The AI Toolkit page explains how each one works.

items.q: Does Vibhor mentor designers or run workshops?
items.a: Yes. He is a design mentor on ADPList, where he has completed 33 one-to-one sessions of 60 minutes each. He also teaches workshops and joins talks and panels on AI in design and design leadership, including GrowthSchool, Designland and the IIIT-Delhi E-Summit.

items.q: Where is he based, and how do I get in touch?
items.a: Vibhor is based in Bengaluru, India, with roots in Jaipur, and works in English and Hindi. The quickest way to reach him is email at onlyvibhor@gmail.com, or LinkedIn at linkedin.com/in/onlyvibhor.
